info.name: Enerza API
info.description:
Load-shedding and power-outage management API (25 endpoints).

**How to use**
1. Set `baseUrl` (default `http://localhost:5000/api/v1`) and, if your seed used different ones, `adminEmail` / `adminPassword`.
2. Run the three *Login as …* requests in **Auth**: they save `adminToken`, `technicianToken` and `customerToken`.
3. Run the folders top to bottom. Requests save the ids later requests need (`feederId`, `scheduleId`, `outageId`, `billId`, `paymentId`).

The collection's pre-request script looks up the seeded grid ids (`zoneId`, `substationId`, `areaId`, …) from the public feeder list and sets `{{tomorrow}}` and `{{thisMonth}}` in Asia/Dhaka time.

Every request has one saved example, and each folder also has error examples (400, 401, 403, 404 and 409 are all covered). Lists inside the examples are shortened to their first entry. They were recorded from a freshly seeded database; tokens are redacted, the bKash gateway was simulated for the payment examples, and no email was sent.

For the multipart requests, pick your own image file in the `profilePhoto` / `photo` field.

**Response format**
- success: `{ success: true, statusCode, message, data, meta? }`
- error: `{ success: false, statusCode, message, errors: [{ path, message }] }`

request.description: Creates a customer account with its service connection (area + meter) and sends a welcome email. `areaId` is filled in by the collection's pre-request script (Pallabi).

response.name: 409 Email already registered
response.body: {"success":false,"statusCode":409,"message":"User with this email already exists","errors":[{"path":"email","message":"Email is already registered"}]}

request.description: Saves `adminToken`. The admin account is created by the seed from `ADMIN_EMAIL` / `ADMIN_PASSWORD`; set the collection variables `adminEmail` and `adminPassword` to match.
Saves `technicianToken` (the Dhaka South technician).
Saves `customerToken` and `refreshToken` (customer2, a commercial connection in Dhanmondi 27).

Body: `{ idToken }`, the ID token the browser gets from Google Sign-In for this app's `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`. A valid token logs the customer in (creating the account on first use) and returns the same shape as the password login. A real token cannot be stored in a collection, so only the error cases are saved here.

response.name: 401 Invalid Google token
response.body: {"success":false,"statusCode":401,"message":"Invalid or expired Google ID token","errors":[{"path":"","message":"Invalid or expired Google ID token"}]}

request.description: Takes the refresh token from the body or from the `refreshToken` cookie.
Any logged-in user. Never returns the password.

Customer: `name`, `contactNumber`, `address`, `areaId`, `meterNumber`. Technician: `name`, `contactNumber`, `isAvailable` (on / off duty).

To set a profile photo, send `multipart/form-data` instead of JSON: the image in `profilePhoto` (JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB) and, optionally, the other fields as JSON in a text field named `data`. The image is stored on Cloudinary and the previous one is removed.

request.description: Plans a fair rotation for a zone or a substation: CRITICAL feeders are never shed, LOW goes before NORMAL before HIGH, and within a priority the feeder shed least in the last 7 days goes first. No feeder is cut in two slots in a row or for more than 4 hours a day. `dryRun: true` (the default) only returns the plan; `false` saves it as DRAFT schedules.

response.name: 200 Dry run: the plan, nothing saved

request.description: Admin: every schedule, filtered by `type`, `status`, `phase` (UPCOMING / ONGOING / COMPLETED), `feederId`, `zoneId`, `from`, `to`. Customer: the published upcoming and ongoing schedules of their own feeder. `phase` is computed from the clock on every read.
`PUBLISHED` (from DRAFT) or `CANCELLED` (with an optional `reason`). Publishing emails a notice to the customers on that feeder. Audited.

Customer: `{ description }`; the feeder comes from their area. `data.outcome` is one of `NEW_OUTAGE_CREATED`, `LINKED_TO_EXISTING_OUTAGE` or `EXPLAINED_BY_SCHEDULE`. Admin: `{ description, feederId }` logs an incident directly. The feeder row is locked, so a feeder never has two open outages. Saves `outageId`.

A customer can attach a photo of the fault by sending `multipart/form-data`: `description` as a text field and the image in `photo` (JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 5 MB). It is stored on Cloudinary and returned as `report.photoUrl`.

request.description: The state machine: REPORTED → ASSIGNED → IN_PROGRESS → RESOLVED, with CANCELLED from REPORTED or ASSIGNED and reassignment from ASSIGNED or IN_PROGRESS. Admin: `ASSIGNED` (optional `technicianId`; without it the least-loaded available technician in the zone is picked) and `CANCELLED` (`note` required). Assigned technician: `IN_PROGRESS` and `RESOLVED` (`note` required). Every move writes a timeline row and an audit row. When an outage is resolved, the customers who reported it are emailed.

request.description: Units = `currentReading` − the customer's last reading. Residential connections use the slab tariff (each slice of units at its own slab's rate), commercial ones a flat rate; then a demand charge per kW and 5% VAT. Calculated in integer paisa. One bill per customer per month. The customer is emailed the bill. `customerId` is saved by *Get my profile*; `{{thisMonth}}` by the pre-request script. Saves `billId`.

response.name: 409 Month already billed
response.body: {"success":false,"statusCode":409,"message":"A bill for 2026-10 has already been issued to this customer (ENZ-BILL-202610-D6938B39)","errors":[{"path":"billingMonth","message":"Already billed"}]}

request.description: Customer: their own bills. Admin: all, filtered by `status`, `billingMonth`, `customerId`, `overdue`. Every bill carries its payment attempts (this is how a payment's status is tracked) and a computed `isOverdue`.

For the customer's own UNPAID bill. Older pending attempts for the bill are expired, a PENDING payment is created, and bKash returns the checkout page as `paymentUrl`. Open it in a browser and pay with the sandbox wallet `01770618575`, OTP `123456`, PIN `12121`; bKash then redirects to the callback. Limited to 5 attempts a minute per customer. Saves `paymentId` and `bkashPaymentId`.

request.description: bKash redirects the customer's browser here, so there is no token. `status=success` is never trusted on its own: the server executes the payment with bKash (falling back to a status query) and settles only when bKash reports code `0000`, `Completed` and the billed amount. Payment PENDING → PAID and bill UNPAID → PAID are conditional updates in one transaction, so opening the same URL again changes nothing. The customer is emailed a receipt once.

Users by role, open outages by status and priority, feeders being load-shed right now, MTTR and SAIFI / SAIDI (overall and per zone) for the last 30 days, revenue this month and the unpaid and overdue totals. Cached in Redis for 5 minutes (`X-Cache` header); writes that change the numbers clear it.
